root_causes.description: The checkout container was killed and recreated during the incident window ('Killing: Container checkout definition changed, will be restarted'), taking the service offline. Server-side request rate collapsed to zero (p50=0.000 req/s) while server-side error rate stayed at 0.000 — the signature of a dead pod whose traffic fails at callers (frontend, accounting, fraud-detection) rather than at the server. Recovery was prolonged by ImagePullBackOff on the pause image.

evidence.query_or_id: Killing: Container checkout definition changed, will be restarted
evidence.observed_value: count=1 during window; followed by Created (count=2) and Started (count=2) container events confirming pod recreation
evidence.expected_baseline: No Killing/restart events for checkout pods in steady state

evidence.observed_value: count=4; Back-off pulling image "gcr.io/google-containers/pause:latest" (count=4), ErrImagePull (count=3), DeadlineExceeded rpc errors (count=3)
evidence.expected_baseline: No image pull failures; pause image cached and pulls succeed

evidence.observed_value: request_rate mean=0.018, p50=0.000, p95=0.057, max=0.057 req/s — service effectively not serving for most of the window
evidence.expected_baseline: Continuous nonzero checkout request rate throughout the window

evidence.observed_value: error_rate mean=0.000, max=0.000 across entire window
evidence.expected_baseline: error_rate < 0.01; zero server-side errors combined with zero traffic confirms the pod was down rather than erroring

evidence.observed_value: anomaly window [1789544081.978→1789544141.978], max=25333760 bytes vs p50=548864 bytes — series discontinuity consistent with pod kill/recreation at incident start
evidence.expected_baseline: Flat, continuous memory series with no anomaly window

root_causes.description: A memory anomaly window was detected at the start of the incident (max 25.3MB vs p50 548KB), which could indicate memory pressure around the crash; however, no OOMKilled event was observed and absolute values are small, so this is more consistent with pod recreation than an OOM kill.

evidence.expected_baseline: Stable memory profile with no anomaly window

evidence.query_or_id: Killing: Container checkout definition changed, will be restarted
evidence.observed_value: Kill event attributed to definition change, not OOMKilled; no OOMKilled events present in the checkout event list
evidence.expected_baseline: An OOMKilled event would be required to confirm memory_stress as the primary cause

root_causes.description: The pause-image ImagePullBackOff (DeadlineExceeded pulling gcr.io/google-containers/pause:latest) prolonged the outage after the container kill, indicating an image-registry/network issue during pod recovery that extended downtime beyond the initial crash.

evidence.query_or_id: Failed to pull image "gcr.io/google-containers/pause:latest": rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = failed to pull a
evidence.observed_value: count=2 (plus ErrImagePull count=3, ImagePullBackOff count=4, BackOff count=4)
evidence.expected_baseline: Image pulls succeed or image is cached; no ErrImagePull/BackOff events

remediation_steps: Audit deployment/config changes to checkout around 2026-09-16T07:34 UTC ('definition changed, will be restarted' indicates a spec change or forced restart) and roll back the offending change if identified.
Pre-pull or mirror gcr.io/google-containers/pause:latest (and all demo images) to a local registry to eliminate ImagePullBackOff/DeadlineExceeded delays during pod recovery.
Add alerting on checkout request_rate==0 and on Killing/BackOff pod events, since server-side error metrics stay at 0 when the pod is dead and will not fire.
Verify checkout memory requests/limits and monitor for OOMKilled events; no OOM was observed this window, but confirm the restart was not resource-driven.
Add redundancy (multiple checkout replicas) so a single pod kill does not take the checkout path fully offline for its callers (frontend, accounting, fraud-detection).
